tier_hierarchy_md:
## Adobe Journey Optimizer — learning tiers

1. **Orientation** — What Journey Optimizer is, how it works, key terminology, role-based paths, and navigating the interface. The entry point for every learner.
2. **Audiences, profiles & data foundations** — Who you target and the data model behind them. Profiles, audiences, and datasets are referenced by every journey, campaign, and message, so they come early.
3. **Content authoring core** — Personalization, templates, fragments, dynamic and multilingual content, AI generation, and content experiments. The reusable material that channels deliver.
4. **Communication channels** — Per-channel creation, design, and configuration (email, in-app, push, SMS/MMS/RCS, direct mail, web, code-based, content cards, inbox, WhatsApp, LINE, live activities). Builds on content and audience skills.
5. **Journeys** — Event-driven orchestration: building, managing, and using activities and expressions to send the channel messages built earlier, plus loyalty challenges.
6. **Campaigns** — Action, API-triggered, and orchestrated campaigns: the batch/triggered delivery model alongside journeys.
7. **Decision capabilities** — Offer decisioning, ranking, AI models, decision policies, offer management, and APIs, layered on top of content and orchestration.
8. **Test, approve & deliver** — Previewing, testing, approving, and resolving conflicts/prioritization before content goes live.
9. **Reporting & monitoring** — Live and all-time reports, custom reports, deliverability monitoring, and troubleshooting of executions.
10. **Configuration & administration** — Channel, journey, event, data-source, and action configuration, system integrations, sandboxes, access control, and privacy/consent. Cross-cutting administrative work.
